title: Claude Code: Dynamic Workflows & Agent Management
content:
## Overview

The 2026 Claude Code updates introduced a tier of agentic infrastructure that goes well beyond single-session coding assistance. Dynamic Workflows, the Agent View CLI interface, and Auto Mode together represent a shift from "AI pair programmer" to "AI engineering team."

---

## Dynamic Workflows

Dynamic Workflows is a research preview feature available on **Enterprise, Team, and Max plans**.

**What it does:** A single Claude Code session can spawn and coordinate **hundreds of parallel subagents** simultaneously. Each subagent works independently on a scoped subtask; the coordinator merges results.

**Primary use case:** Codebase-scale migrations. Example: upgrading an entire monorepo from one framework version to another — each subagent handles a subset of files, the coordinator detects conflicts, and the whole migration runs in a fraction of the time a sequential approach would require.

**How it differs from the existing multi-agent support:** Prior multi-agent features in Claude Code allowed spawning a handful of subagents sequentially or in small parallel batches. Dynamic Workflows removes the practical ceiling and adds a coordination layer that handles scheduling, result aggregation, and conflict detection automatically.

**Status:** Research preview as of June 2026. Available to Enterprise/Team/Max subscribers; not yet on Pro or individual plans.

---

## Agent View (CLI)

Agent View is a new CLI panel for managing concurrent sessions:

- **Start agents** in the background without blocking the terminal
- **Peek at status and last responses** for any running agent without switching focus
- **Jump into sessions** only when input is required — agents run autonomously until they need a decision
- **Background agents** continue running even when you're not actively in their session window

This addresses a practical pain point: previously, running multiple Claude Code sessions required multiple terminal windows with no unified view. Agent View consolidates them into one interface.

---

## Auto Mode

Auto Mode, now available on the **Pro plan** (alongside Opus, in addition to the existing Max plan rollout), changes how Claude Code handles permissions:

**Old behavior:** Claude Code would pause and prompt for approval before any potentially risky action — file writes, shell commands, git operations.

**Auto Mode behavior:**
- **Routine actions** (reading files, running linters, making git commits on non-main branches) run without interrupting the user
- **Destructive or suspicious actions** (force pushes, `rm -rf`, credential access, outbound network requests to unknown hosts) are blocked and surfaced for review
- Safety checks run in the background rather than blocking the main thread

Model support: Auto Mode works with both **Sonnet 4.6** and **Opus** models.

---

## Fast Mode Pricing Update

Fast Mode — which uses Claude Opus with optimized output generation — dropped significantly in price:

| | Previous | Updated |
|---|---|---|
| Input | ~$30/M tokens | **$10/M tokens** |
| Output | ~$150/M tokens | **$50/M tokens** |

This is approximately a 3× cost reduction, making Fast Mode viable for higher-throughput agentic workloads that previously defaulted to Sonnet for cost reasons.

---

## Visual Output

Claude Code can now generate **interactive visual artifacts** directly in the session:

- Interactive charts and data visualizations
- Architectural diagrams
- Mobile app prototypes (interactive)

These render in the Claude Code web interface and can be exported or embedded. This extends the tool beyond code into the adjacent deliverables developers typically context-switch to other tools for.

---

## Skills and Plugins

The 2026 updates expanded the plugin/skills system:

- **Security-guidance plugin** — built-in awareness of OWASP top-10 patterns and common misconfigurations; warns during code generation when generated code exhibits vulnerable patterns
- **Background jobs** — skills and hooks can now run as background jobs that report back when complete, rather than blocking the session
- **Browser selection** — choose which browser engine Claude uses for web-based tasks (relevant for computer-use and web scraping workflows)
